terms.meaning: The period over which a process's benefit grows from nothing to its full level.
The share of full benefit that is actually delivered inside the window.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose of the adoption ramp
sections.what: Explains that each process's benefit ramps up in a straight line after it starts, rather than all at once. The ramp is applied per process before totals are made. The file also sets the twelve-month window that every figure uses.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: applying a ramp after totals creates a step change that no single process shows, and an exact formula keeps output the same on every run.
sections.watch_out: The twelve-month window is an assumption that changes how comparable figures are, so changing it alters every benefit figure.

sections.name: realised_fraction
sections.title: Share of benefit inside the window
sections.what: Works out what share of full benefit a process actually delivers in the first twelve months, given when it starts and how long it takes to ramp up. The result is a fraction between zero and one.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: start time and ramp are combined in one calculation, so their overlap is not counted twice.
sections.watch_out: A negative ramp raises an error, and a start at or after the window returns zero. Callers must expect both results.

summary: Works out the share of a process's benefit that arrives within the first twelve months, using a straight-line ramp that starts at the process's start month.
purpose: Turns a start month and a ramp length into one fraction, which then multiplies the process's benefit.
why: The ramp is applied per process because a single portfolio-level ramp does not match how real processes behave. An exact formula keeps output identical on every run.
how: Take the months left in the twelve-month window after the start. If none are left, return zero. If the ramp is zero, return the full share. Otherwise use one formula if the ramp finishes inside the window, and another if it does not. Divide by the window length.
inputs: The ramp length in months and the start month, counted from the start of the run.
outputs: A fraction between zero and one.
risks: Wrong units, such as years entered as months, silently scale the benefit. The window is fixed at twelve months and is not adjustable here.
debug: If benefit looks too low, check the start month and ramp months passed in. A negative ramp raises an error, which means the input is bad. Check the wave start months in the phasing file.
